headline: Reproducible workflows for barcode and microbial function inference from sequencing data
label: Sequence Analysis Workflow Tools
summary: Four recent preprints package long-read and metabarcoding analysis as containerized, reproducible tools running from raw reads to annotations or barcodes.
synthesis: The common thread is packaging sequence-based inference as reproducible, workflow-level software that runs from raw reads to a defined output. BIP and MAP both use containerized workflows: BIP converts FASTQ output into COI DNA barcodes, separating target from non-target sequences and assigning BINs, while MAP provides a Docker-installable metabarcoding workflow for highly multiplexed, replicated designs with long-read COI features. seqsizzle addresses the upstream step, offering a Rust terminal interface for visualizing long-read FASTQ/FASTA data with fuzzy primer matching and k-mer enrichment to decode barcode and adapter architectures. MagicLamp applies a different target, HMM-based annotation of specialized microbial metabolic functions, through a command-line toolkit and web server. What is new is the attention to long-read barcode and adapter architecture within end-to-end workflows, alongside targeted annotation of microbial functions.
